entries.title: Selected words can be added to the glossary
entries.body: On your own articles, selecting words in the text offers Add to glossary beside highlight and comment, with a mouse or on a touch screen. If the glossary already has that term, its entry opens; if not, the Glossary panel opens and looks it up, adding it once the answer is written. It is offered only when the article's glossary is ready and the selection is short enough to be a term.

entries.title: Quiz questions appear in the margin
entries.body: On your own articles, when Marginalia is on screen and the article has no quiz yet, the app writes one, and its questions appear as notes in the margin beside the passage each asks about. While the margin shows, the questions sit there instead of between the paragraphs, never in both places. They are there to prompt you to stop and reflect as you read.

entries.title: Small screens show a reminder of the article
entries.body: On a phone or a small or short window, scrolling back up once the article's heading is off screen shows a strip at the top with the title, authors, date and estimated reading time, and on your own articles how much you have read. It slides away as you scroll on, and is hidden while a mode's panel is open.

entries.title: Ideas is written when you open it
entries.body: When you add an article, the app no longer prepares Ideas along with everything else. The list of ideas the piece assumes is written the first time you open the Ideas mode, so that first visit waits while it is written.

entries.title: Bibliography catches every work in a citation list
entries.body: When a citation in the text names several works inside one pair of brackets, separated by commas, the bibliography in Sources picks up each of them rather than stopping at the first. A bibliography built before this change gains the missing works only when it is built again.

entries.title: Explanations can be reordered and extended
entries.body: A new Explanations list shows, by default, the places that are both hard and central, in reading order; you can also show all of them, hardest first or most central first. Find more adds places without losing the ones you have, and the list uses the panel's full width. Explanations is behind the Experimental features switch on your profile page.

entries.title: Your own words use a quieter handwriting
entries.body: Your comments, notes and questions are drawn in a different handwritten typeface. It still sets your words apart from the author's, but is less over the top than the one before.
